subject: Credit redemption window & contract carve-out request
messages:
From: Maya Lee <maya@orbitanalytics.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on promo credits & invoicing window

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to trial Redwood. Before we sign the SOW, finance asked for a couple of clarifications around the accelerator credits you mentioned:

1) Redemption window: can the free credits be activated in two phases (50% at contract execution, 50% on first production deployment) or do they need a single activation date?
2) Tax treatment: we operate in multiple states — will Redwood issue a single credit line item on the invoice or separate credit adjustments?
3) Contract carve-out: we may need the credits excluded from the committed usage calculation for the first 90 days. Is that a standard exception?

I attached the latest SOW (Orbit_SOW_v3.pdf) and a short usage snapshot from our POC (orbit_onboarding_usage_Q1.csv) to help.

Can you loop in your billing or legal folks as needed? We need to finalize by the end of next week to hit our internal onboarding window.

Best,
Maya
Director of Cloud Platform
Orbit Analytics

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Maya Lee <maya@orbitanalytics.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on promo credits & invoicing window

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list and for the attachments. Quick answers below; I copied Ben (sales lead) and Irene (billing/legal) to confirm the carve-out language.

Summary answers (high level):
- Redemption window: flexible. We can do a two-phase activation (50/50) — common for accelerator partnerships. We will record activation timestamps to avoid double-counting.
- Tax / invoicing: we issue a single invoice per billing period. Credits show as a line-item credit; tax is applied per your billing address. For multi-state operations we can provide an alternate invoice breakdown if required by your accounting team.
- Contract carve-out: 90-day exclusion from committed usage is not standard but is doable as a short-term amendment. Legal will need to add a clause to the SOW.

Next steps I propose:
1) Irene reviews the SOW and drafts a one-paragraph carve-out amendment (ETA: EOD 5/13).
2) Ben and I confirm the activation mechanics and update the SOW appendix with activation dates.
3) If that looks good, we send the DocuSign link for signature and set a kickoff (onboarding) date.

Is the 50/50 activation acceptable? If yes I will flag it for the amendment.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Maya Lee <maya@orbitanalytics.io>
Date: 2027-05-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on promo credits & invoicing window

Hi all — quick legal/billing note after reviewing Orbit_SOW_v3.pdf.

I agree with Rachel that we can support:
- A split activation (50/50) recorded by activation event timestamps. We will add precise language so the credits cannot be reactivated or backdated.
- A 90-day carve-out from committed usage calculations. Proposed insertion: "Promotional credits issued under this Agreement shall be excluded from committed usage calculations for a period of ninety (90) days following the first activation event, provided such credits are used solely for the Purpose described in the SOW and are not transferred or refunded."

A couple of operational clarifications for Orbit finance:
• Credits will appear as a single negative line on monthly invoices until exhausted. If you need state-by-state tax breakdown for reconciliation, we can produce an itemized credit report on request (additional bookkeeping service).
• We recommend Orbit confirm a primary billing address to determine tax jurisdiction; absent that, we use the address in the SOW.

If everyone is aligned I'll prepare the amendment and push the SOW to DocuSign (I can include an option to split activation dates). ETA for the draft amendment: tomorrow morning (5/14).

—Irene
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Lee <maya@orbitanalytics.io>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-14T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on promo credits & invoicing window

Maya — happy to confirm the commercial side. A few operational notes so onboarding goes smoothly:

- Activation events: for the 50/50 plan we need you to identify the "first production deployment" owner (name + email) who will approve the second activation. That ensures we don't auto-activate the second tranche prematurely.
- Kickoff timeline: once signed, our onboarding lead will run a 2-week onboarding plan. Can Orbit target June 1 as the production deployment target?
- Credits visibility: we'll add a line to the Redwood Console billing dashboard so your finance and engineering leads can track credit consumption in real time.

If that works, Irene will drop the amendment into DocuSign and we’ll share the HubSpot deal record for signature tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/342/DEAL-2027-ORBIT-342

Thanks — looking forward to getting Orbit live.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Orbit_SOW_v3.pdf (attached), orbit_onboarding_usage_Q1.csv (attached)
